text:
Tragedy of Veyska
Forgive me, Mother. I only sought to belong. Let your wandering child come home.

Tragedy of Veyska
Legends say Veyska never found rest. The Moon Tribe turned her away, and she was forever lost, condemned to wander by the bitter curse. The stolen riches became a burden on her soul so great that she buried them deep within the mountain's stone. When she finally succumbed to the cold, her body fell, but her cursed soul remained bound to the lantern, still searching, endlessly, for the hearth she could not claim.

Tragedy of Veyska
Beneath the chill gaze of the Harvest Moon, where the cliffs stand tallest and the air holds a stillness unnatural, a child was found in a basket of black pine.

Tragedy of Veyska
Let the treasure be returned to its rightful place.
Only one free of greed may lift the curse.
Else the lantern shall rise again, and the soul shall wander still.

Tragedy of Veyska
The threshold—that sacred line between Possession and Freedom—was where she was caught. The Keeper stood there, backlit by the flickering oil lamp of the vault, her face a mask of bitter injury. Veyska did not speak; the word "Mother" was a cold stone in her throat. She only ran, clutching the heavy sack of treasure and holding aloft the stolen Lantern.

And the Keeper, the guardian of all things lost, did not scream or weep. She merely raised a withered hand, and her voice, low and sharp as shattering ice, cast the binding:

“May your soul wander with your betrayal, never resting, never home.”

Tragedy of Veyska
One night, when the Moon was a silver blade, Veyska crept through the passages, her feet silent on the cold stone. She gathered her mother’s brightest treasures and her prized artifacts, and at the last, she took the Lantern.

Tragedy of Veyska
Veyska lived within the Vault of Silence. She was groomed and guarded, her days spent in the dim, stale light of ancient gold, protected by her mother’s fierce, possessive love. Yet, though she had warmth and comfort, her heart longed for something more. Each night, she would gaze up at the wandering Moon, and know that her true home lay beyond the vault.

Tragedy of Veyska
The truth, like moss on a forgotten stone, grew slowly. Veyska learned of the Moon Tribe—outcasts who scorned the static world, embracing only change and the rhythm of the tides, surely she was one of them. But to be accepted by them, she knew she could not arrive empty-handed. She needed a sign of her belonging, a tribute of great worth—a gift that could only be stolen.

The Vault held countless glories, but one treasure was most sacred to the Keeper: the Ghost Lantern. They said its bronze was taken from a fallen star, and that it had belonged to the Moon Tribe long ago, pulsing with their blue, restless light.

Tragedy of Veyska
She was taken not by a shepherd or a kind soul, but by the Keeper of Forgotten Things—a woman, a curator who dwelt among hoards of relics, treasures, and the sealed histories of the world. The Keeper did not love; she collected. And so she took the child, named her Veyska, and set her among the gleaming artifacts as if she were the rarest, most priceless of them all.

Pieth
Memory, the white raven Guardian, Keeper of the Past, whispers to me all he has witnessed.  Against the vastness of his knowledge, my troubles seem insignificant, like distant stars in an endless night sky.

Pieth
I have learned that Grimnir once was a skilled and well traveled shaman. He possessed extensive knowledge about all the tribes and even realms beyond our own.

Pieth
I am filled with grief for the fate of my people. I share my pain with Memory, the wise white raven, my great teacher and dear friend. I can see Memory embodies my sorrow.  My pain is now his to bear.

Pieth
Despite his numerous spiritual talents, the Council of Elders deemed Grimnir unfit for their order. They instructed him to go back to his homeland and utilize his abilities to uplift the Bear Tribe from poverty. Only then would he be considered worthy of their order.

Pieth
Memory tells me of a war raging south of Misthaven. The shaman Grimnir has awoken the Bear Guardian, infecting it’s spirit with a sickness from beyond our realm. How far will he go? Are we safely beyond his reach?

Grimnir
In Misthaven there dwelleth a lesser raven, named Thought. Lock her away, she is of no use to us.

Pieth
As I take my final breaths, I see Memory growing into a monstrous form, embodying all our rage and pain. His eyes glow red and his breathing is labored. He has broken through the dungeon roof and has set flight towards his temple, where the Bear Tribe is camped.

Pieth
The mist brings me great comfort. It blankets the land like a veil, concealing my tribe from the dangers beyond our borders.  Though Grimnir’s War rages, we have gone unnoticed for many years.

Isölda
I dreamt a fox came to me in my cell. It's light was strong and the darkness recoiled at its presence. It continued on to the Great Library, the brooding lair of our fallen guardian. And then I woke. What sort of tale is this? Either I am a seer or I am drifting into madness.

Gwyna
The fox with healing light will cleanse the spirits of man and beast.

Grimnir
Memory, the White Raven, guardian of the past, is of great use to me.  For memories can be tainted and the past can become a bottomless vessel of sorrow, regret and shame.

Feon
Great Guardian spirits, forgive my anger and my silence. Send one to do what we could not. Rejoin me to my companions and gather the melodies we foolishly cast away. Let the music rise once more to unveil the Lost Aurorian Light. Let us sing together in the echo of thy coming.

Mog the Mighty
We can not find the Fox Guardian. Perhaps it has abandoned this world and returned to the forests of light.

Bato the Doubtless
Warriors o’ gerd stature be arrivin’ on our shores from lands far off, hurr. They wear the marks o’ the Bear Tribe, yet also a new emblem ol’ Bato don't rightly know. We be welcomin’ ‘em openly an' sharin' o’ our abundance, for 'tis the way o' the Stag, it be. Ho hurr!

Eyma
It was Feon who first placed the lyre into my hands, proving that its worth lay not in the beautiful frame, but in it's song. He showed me that a voice is not merely for speaking, but for soaring. And that the greatest treasures we could steal are the melodies hidden around us.
So with new companions I now search the world for these Lost Melodies.

Feon
That man Grimöl possesses a passion that is as dangerous as it is raw. Despite all his cravings, he hath no taste for song. He knoweth not what beauty is; he seeks only to possess the beauty that finds him.

I see Eyma watching him, the way he moves with a wild, simple power. My heart is troubled. What could she possibly see in a man so base? A man who loveth not the song cannot be trusted with the singer. The Lost Melodies seem suddenly very far away.

Feon
The aurora
is a song the eyes can see, though the ears have forgotten.
And where upon the earth have these notes fallen?
I have seen it
in my dreams, the lights cast from the night sky,
and bards undaunted, their destinies tied.
Set forth to find
Through a tragic journey, the lost melodies to which they're bound:
the lost auroria, both the light and the sound.

Bato the Doubtless
The music be ceased, an' the silence be heavy, burr... Our Eyma be gone, fled to bind ‘er life to that man Grimöl, carryin' a secret that’s torn ‘er from Feon. I watched ‘er drop ‘er Lyre into the dark waters beneath the theater; it sank to the deeps without a plea. She looked back an' all us saw be a girl conflicted with tears in ‘er eyes. I will miss ‘er laughter an' ‘er witty humor, for she were like a sister to me, she were.

I tries to cheer up Feon with a bit o' jokin', but he cut us back hard. I don't blame ‘im, though. He’s just lost the love o' 'is life, he has. Where we go from 'ere, I don't rightly know. Burr hmph...

Bato the Doubtless
Feon be lost without Eyma. Without ‘er sweet melody, I fear ‘is heart has no reason to beat. Though our halls be silent, they be filled with a bitter sadness, hurr. Ol' Bato’s heart be heavy as stone seein' a friend so broken.

Bato the Doubtless
The road be long, but the company be better! Moi friend Feon’s got 'is head in the clouds an' 'is eyes on the stars, but down 'ere on the moss, we’re havin' ourselves a roight proper feast o' songs! We be gatherin' Lost Melodies from all the Northern Isles. From whispers in the woods to the call o’ the mountains. Every note we find makes the world feel a bit brighter, hurr. I’ve never seen Eyma so radiant; she plays ‘er lyre an' the very birds stop to listen. Feon be smitten by ‘er, he be, though he’d never say it plain. He has to put everythin' into poetry, layered with all them metaphors. I confess, half the things he says go roight over ol' Bato's head! There ain't a doubt in moine mind, as long as the three o' us stand together, we’re gonna find that Lost Aurorian Light. 'Tis a grand thing, walkin' the world with your truest companions, oh ho!

Eyma
A bird may love the sky with all its heart,
From clouds and starlight, it would never part.
Yet every wing grows weary of the blue,
And seeks the mud when mind's tired and body too.
To touch the sky is a noble, wondrous thing,
But the heavy soil does not demand a wing.
And though a bird will always fly best,
the earth is where it comes to rest.

Eyma
My mind drifts as this fever takes hold, yet a single truth presses through the haze. I fled from thee once, Feon, fearing the secret I carried was not thine to share, or perhaps I feared it was. Shame is a quiet room with no windows. Now, as the world thins, I see thy likeness in the boy’s eyes. I cannot tell if it is a cruel trick of memory or a final clarity. Let the Guardians judge the harmony of it. Forgive me Feon, the love that belonged to thee is now a lost melody.

Kai Lalu
Where are the Tribes of the North? We sailed far, yet their shores lie empty. If a friend in need finds these words, know we have left a gift. Seek it, return it, and aid will rise from the deep.

Eyma
Within me is a steady rhythm yet to grow; born of me and of another. I fear one day the music will stop, and I shall be left holding the most difficult note alone

Eyma
I chanced upon two bards camped beneath the stars, their camp littered with instruments so fine they seemed carved from the dreams of the world. The most radiant was a lyre, adorned with the image of a rising sun. I took it, thinking such a prize wasted on sleeping men.
I had nearly reached the shadows when a voice drifted through the dark. 'Thou mayest take the hollow wood and the strings,' the bard remarked, never even rising, 'but its true value thou lackest the wit to steal.' I drew my blade, but he did not reach for his. He merely gestured toward the fire. 'Come, stay but a moment, and I shall teach thee to find the treasure thou hast missed.'

Feon
She is gone. Bato says I should follow her, but follow her where? Into the arms of that drunkard? Into the chaos she hath chosen? She hath abandoned our quest, our destiny. She hath abandoned me. And soon Bato shall leave too.

There is a darkness growing in the air, a bitterness I have never felt before. Our trio is broken and the melodies shall remain lost. My drum sounds empty and without rhythm. I shall hide it deep within these caverns where the darkness can swallow its light, for I have no more songs to sing.

Bato the Doubtless
All gerd things come to a closin', hurr... even the songs. Our liddle band be naught but dust, an' moi belly be a-rumblin'. I be off to work in the Mosswood moines. A bit o' diggin' an' a bit o' sootin'. It ain't the music o' moi friends, no’at, but the sound o' iron on stone be better’n the silence Feon has joined 'imself to.
Burr... moi flute stays ‘ere, now sleepin' in the roots o' that ol' tree. I feels to one day return an' play ‘er once more. Again with moi friends, laughin' an' a-singin'. Ho hurr, one day no doubt!

Mog the Mighty
Mosswood burns and their Guardian is defeated.  We now turn our attention to Stormvale, the fortified highlands of the Ram Tribe.

Mog the Mighty
We have landed on northern coast of Mosswood forest, the home to the Stag Tribe. Despite we being heavily armed the people here foolishly welcome us.  They must yet be unaware of our plan to besiege their great city.  We await Grimnir’s signal fires from the south before we lay waste to their homes.

Arkenmar
We've captured the Moon Wolf Guardian, in hopes to quell the strife between the wolf packs. May this act cause the Moon Pack to peacefully submit to our rule and unite with us against Grimnir, just as the Moon submits to the glory of the Sun each day.

Fennuk
Ha! Grimnir, the deceitful knave, hath betrayed us, and our Guardian Wolf, the master of deceit, now sickened by his foul plague. Blinded by his lies, we failed to see the corruption rooted in his soul. Aye, he may have dwelt amongst us, but he is kin to us no more. Oh, the folly of one who seeks to deceive the masters of deceit! Thirsting for vengeance, we shall not rest until he rues the day he crossed us.

Arkenmar
What deceit hath Grimnir sown among the Moon Warriors, provoking their unjust assault upon us? We, rightful stewards of the mountains, akin to the sun's dominion over the earth, sustain ourselves without taking from others. They, cloaked in glacial refuge, are but thieves ignorant of true sovereignty, mere reflections of our unwavering example. Without our guiding light, they dwell in darkness, bereft of our radiant wisdom.

Grimnir
The Stag Guardian nutures and cares for his people as if they were his own children.  Oh, then how great his pain will be when he witnesses their destruction.  His home will be empty and his kingdom will become a bramble of thorns as anguish chokes his spirit.

Storkush
I hid my relic deep, to elude Grimnir’s grasp. But my efforts were in vain as he's found me here at last. Though my spirit soon wanders from this world, my foe I do forgive. Though I die old and alone, I pray my kin yet live.

Storkush
Word has reached me that the City of Mosswood has been sieged. All survivors now flee north to Stormvale and beyond. I am old and cannot make such a journey. There is nothing I can do now. Perhaps I will go unnoticed deep within these vaults.

Storkush
Stag be praised, the forest provides bountifully for our tribe. We have more food than we could ever need. This old cavern is an excellent store house.

King Kumari
Grimnir has destroyed the bridge to the stone tower. I am unable to regroup with our tribe and assist the Stag Guardian. Perhaps that is what Grimnir wants, for me to remain here with my relic.

King Kumari
I spent the day meditating in the forest and communed with the spirit of the stag Oto-Oksu. His light is gentle and patient. He gifted me with an ancient relic, an antler crown, and taught me that I can walk beyond the constraints of my mortal body, in spirit form.

Grimnir
The Council of Elders are naive to think that there is but one world beyond our own for I have found another.  A place born of anguish and the trials of affliction.  A place that finds strength in pain and solace in suffering.  I Grimmir, the fatherless, lay claim to this realm as my birthright.

Grimnir
In this place of death and sorrow the veil between realms is thin.  I will depart from my body and walk amongst the spirits in the forests of light.  And when I return from this great journey I will surely have place amongst mine elders.

Words of Memory
In ancient days, the 4th and youngest son of Éona, remained close to his mother in her old age. His name was Kotho and he planted an entire forest. His forest became so mighty that even the Stag, Guardian of Life, attended to it.  The people called this forest Mosswood.

King Kumari
I dreamt the forest was veiled with shadow and death. The stag was lost, his eyes were red with hate, and his domain became a bramble of thorns.

King Kumari
I dreamt a fox came to me, long after I had passed. And searched amongst my bones until, it found my crown at last. Then from this tower yonder, back to the city great. It cleansed the noble stag with light and restored his rightly state.

King Kumari
By my word this crypt is sealed and I forbid any to enter.  Let the deeds of him who sought to traverse the void be forgotten and that suffering and hate remain locked away forever.

Lady Amara
We have just returned from trading with the Fox Tribe, our ally on the southern isle. Their craftsmanship is beyond compare. Our relations with them continue to strengthen, bringing prosperity to our Great City.

Lady Amara
The Stag's light is fading under the cruelty of Grimnir.  I remain powerless to cleanse our guardian without my staff. Grimnir has taken it from me and soon he will take my life.  However, death is not the end and I will soon walk in forests of light.

Lady Amara
The council's fears of Grimnir's ill intent are being manifest.  He marches toward our gate in this very moment.  I can only assume he seeks to claim my staff in order to subjugate the Stag Guardian.  We are attempting to escape but it may be too late.

Eyma
I, Eyma of the Moon Pack, now endure my nights in the Sunken City, a fitting stage for an outcast. I nurture my fatherless son, bestowing upon him the name Grimmir. It is a name that tastes of both peace and turmoil, a duality he shall have to carry. Not knowing his birthright, his path will be his own making.

Grimnir
I am Grimmir the fatherless, Child of Sorrow, a spirit betwixt peace and anguish. My home is a dwelling of falsehoods, and my cradle is a cavern of ice, where death, a frequent guest, beckons my kin to leave me.

Mog the Mighty
Grimnir's connections to the Moon Wolf Pack remains strong.  They say he was born here and treat him as one of their own.  He has promised them lordship over the mountains should they join us. They relish the idea of over throwing the Sun Wolf Pack and seem all too eager to perform their mischief.

Mog the Mighty
I fear Grimnir's trust in the Moon Warriors is misplaced.  How can we trust these tricksters? They are master manipulators, liers, and thieves.  I will feel much better once I leave this place.

Fennuk
We are the truth and we are the lie. We are bold but often hide. We wax and wane from time to time, just like the moon in the night sky.

Words of Memory
In ancient days, Valulf, 3rd son of Éona, was lost as a child.  He wandered helplessly in the rugged mountains.  He was found by the Wolf Guardians Esmir and Okamu who raised him in the shelter of a glacier.

Piera
Ascending the tallest peak, I brave the biting cold, for in harsh elements lies the purest test of body and soul. Upon the mountain's throne, the Sun Wolf rightly reigns.  And I must prove the resilience of my own inner-flame.

Words of Memory
From Valulf came the Great Wolf Tribe.  His people honored Okamu, the white wolf guardian of the sun and Esmir, the black wolf guardian of the moon.

Words of Memory
When Valulf died there was a disagreement amongst his children about who should lead the tribe. There was a small skirmish and the eldest daughter Éota prevailed.  The younger son Mirth who had contested his right to rule was banished with his followers.  Thus the Great Wolf Tribe was fractured.

Fennuk
Last night, my hunger led me to a valley where the Ram Tribe's flock grazed. Fortune seemed to smile upon me, for it was only guarded by a small girl. Thinking to steal a sheep or two, I approached, only to be met by a whirlwind of fury. With teeth bared and blades flashing like lightning, she drove me back. Never afore have I witnessed such intensity and resolve. Truly, children of the storm they be.

Feon
Legend speaks of an era of suffering, when the skies are red and the spirits rage. Yet within those tales lies a glimmer of hope, foretelling the return of the lost aurora. Shall I live to witness the foxes paint the sky once more? My heart yearns for that ancient melodic light.

Skogmir the Battle Shaman
Although the Stag and Raven tribes have fallen, the Ram stands resolute upon the hilltop.  The storm clouds blacken as we prepare for war.  Grimnir's armies, shall fall before our walls.

Arkenmar
We are the Wolf Tribe, fractured in days of old. Two halves under one stewardship. Ensnared in an unending dance of hate and mockery.  Our guardians bite and howl, forever pursuing one another across the sky. The sun, in its pursuit, drives the moon from the firmament. And when night descends, it stealthily returns.

Piera
Focus on breathing to calm the beating heart. For a calm heart will settle the mind and a settled mind will unbind the spirit. Just breathe, and the spirit is boundless.

Grimöl
Here lies Grimöl, the wretched.  Unblessed by the bear guardians and drinker of ale. Companion to Eyma of the wolf tribe, and father of Grimmir. Here he lies alone, unclaimed by kin, and far removed from the honorable restgrounds of his people.

Taukara, Daughter of War
In the wake of Grimnir’s treachery, our Guardians falter, their noble spirits tainted by his vile deeds. Yet, from the depths of our collective anguish, arises a solemn vow to them. We that remain from shattered tribes, both young and old, bind ourselves together in an unbreakable oath to defeat Grimnir. Henceforth, we shall be known as the Northguard, the united people of the Northern Isles.

Grimnir
We need not remove the Ram from his hilltop.  Let him remain there. Let him remain in endless combat. Let the rage permeate his soul.

Heilda, Shield Maiden
We are the Ram Tribe, shaped by the rain and weathered by the storm. Like the Ram, our guardian, our feet are firmly planted and we can not be moved.

Grimnir
The Ram Tribe's combative nature shall be their undoing.  They will see this war as a contest of strength and will embrace it.  Let this war consume them slowly.

Rikia the Witch
The Guardians tainted all in red, are bent by Grimnir’s cruel embrace. The age of man shall reach its end, and death will lay claim to this place.

Skogmir the Battle Shaman
Smoke rises from Mosswood, I must swiftly journey to our borders to aid our kin. May the Ram grant us swiftness. My daughter, Taukara, shall guard our flocks in my absence. Woe to any who dare cross her path.

Taukara, Daughter of War
Like a storm in the night I defend my flock from thieving shadows. With swift action and sharp iron, I protect the helpless from the mouth of wolves.  I am shepherd with a warriors heart.

Mog the Mighty
I am Mog the mighty! Mine arm hath the strength of Eynbor and none can bind me. When I rage the earth shakes and mine enemies fall.

Taukara, Daughter of War
Our shaman have fallen and their relics are lost amongst the ruins of our strongholds. The Ram's light fades, his eyes glow with a sickly red. There are none left to cleanse him.

Feon
The age of man is over, and our people are dying. The Guardians are all a sickening red, corrupted by realms beyond. Where is the aurora that once painted the sky? Where is the fox with its healing light? Vanished, it seems, into the night.

Taukara, Daughter of War
I am too young to join the warriors of our tribe. Yet, when the skies blacken and lightning strikes, I can see the battle on our border. Oh, how I long to join them and feel the storms of war.

Isölda
In the archives, whispers tell of an age of woe, when the void shall tear asunder and anguish shall creep into our realm like a sickness. Crimson skies will loom, and guardians shall rage. A world in ruins, consumed by despair, shall await salvation.

Words of Memory
In the ancient days, Hyskar Stormfather, the second son of Éona, settled in the rugged highlands with his family. He bonded with the Ram Guardian and his people became known as the Ram Tribe.

Mog the Mighty
Grimnir’s prowess surpasses even the stoutest warriors. Not even the formidable battle shaman Skogmir could vanquish him, though their clash rent this tower asunder. Skogmir now lies deep within the rubble of this tower, laid low by his own hammer.

Mog the Mighty
We have suffered many losses in capturing this fortress. The Ram Tribe, fearless protectors, boast of a single warrior outmatching a dozen of our own. Yet, notwithstanding their bravery, none can rival the might of Grimnir.

Kai Lalu
The door is simple, if the key you have brought.  Unwelcome you are, for a turtle you are not.

Words of Memory
In ancient days, Runa the eldest daughter of the Éona was a quiet and peculiar child.  She was followed by an old white raven named Memory who told her many things.  Runa with wisdom beyond her years, created Runescript to record all that Memory made known unto her.  Memory and Runa sought solitude far from her mother and sibling. She settled in the far north in a land shrouded in mist, where her vast libraries could be safe.

Grimnir
I seek the final guardian, the legendary Spirit of the North, the fox guardian of the aurora.  Like the others, it too must be perfected through pain.

Eyma
The ale is spent and Grimöl’s temper has turned. Looking at my son, I realize the safety of this house has become its own kind of peril. We cannot stay. 
Yet we can not return to the bards for the shameful way I abandoned them. I’d rather sink into the depths where the drowned are kept secret. And there, hidden below, none will ask for explanations.

Eyma
I have lived long in the shadow of a man who claimed to love me, only to find my own light is the price of his warmth. I remain because the world outside is wide and cold, but it is the silence here that cuts the deepest. Sometimes I begin to hum an old melody, a ghost of a former life, only to choke it back when Grimöl's boots find the threshold. I chose the comfort of the fire, but I neglected to notice the wood has all turned to ash. I miss the lyre’s radiant song, the flute's friendly whistle, and most of all, the steady, guiding beat of the drum.

Words of Memory
Upon the bountiful land the people of Eynbor grew numerous and were known as the Bear Tribe. They lived idle lives in the cradle of peace.  Never wanting for food or drink, never toiling and never contested or provoked.

Grimnir
From sorrow and shame, I shall ascend, forging a path uniquely mine. I will visit all the guardians and seek their blessings.

Mog the Mighty
We the Bear Tribe, son’s of Eynbor, eldest of Éona. Pledge ourselves to Grimnir, the war maker. For he hath awakened the bear as legends foretold and shall lead us into battle and deliver unto us the lands of our birthright.

Words of Memory
In the days of the ancient, the eldest son of Éona, known as Eynbor, grew to be a large and powerful man. He was prone to anger but found peace on the eastern isle, deep inside the warmth of an isolated mountain. There he met his kindred spirit the Bear Guardian, who also loved warmth, food, and peaceful rest.

Fennuk
Oh Grimnir, that treacherous fool who dared to outwit the masters of moon and mischief, now treads unwittingly into a snare I have deftly woven. He imagines that the Northguard shall bend to his will, but alas, 'tis not so. For he walks to his execution.

Grimnir
The Northguard have surrendered. I sail to the isle of the Fox Tribe to take my position at the head of the Council of Elders.

Omol the Abandoned
Grimnir hath been executed by the Northguard and the war hath ceased. Yet the guardians rage on and there are none left to cleanse them.  Scarlet plague fills the air and chokes our bodies and poisons our spirits.

Rikia the Witch
Where lies the aurora's radiant hue, adorning night skies in greens and blues? Where roams the fox, in distant far lands? Or has it returned to heal the guardians?

Omol the Abandoned
From the sky, the Ravens witness our ill deeds and our fate is sealed. Atop the hills the Ram splinters our shields with fierce lightning, and in the forest below the Stag entangles our feet with thorns. The Bear in fury shakes the earth and our cities crumble while Wolves wander our paths devouring our children.  Following Grimnir was folly; our end draws near.

Rikia the Witch
Behold! Grimnir, son of the mighty Bear Tribe, rouses the Bear Guardian from his age old slumber, heralding a new era!  The awakening of the bear foretells a time of war, where the Bear Tribe no longer sits idly within their homeland but claims the birthright of Eynbor, the entirety of the Northern Isles.

Grimnir
I am Grimnir the War Maker. Too long hath the Bear slept deep within his mountain.  I will descend into the depths of the earth and find his resting place among the halls of molten stone.  I will awaken him and shall be his master. Destruction shall flow from me and all will know my name.

Omol the Abandoned
Our tribe departs to lay claim to lands beyond. Yet, old and crippled, I remain, pondering: Are we of noble heart or ensnared by deceit?

Isölda
Long after the 6 tribes have fallen, the fox guardian shall return with healing light and restore it’s kindred guardians. Then pass through these halls triumphantly onward to cleanse the fallen heir of Éona.

Balgair
In my day, a shaman called Grimnir of the Bear Tribe broke the peace between tribes and began a great and terrible war. Those true to the old alliance united and fought against him.

Taukara, Daughter of War
For his atrocities, Grimnir was sentenced to death and the war ceased. Yet the land bore the stain of his ill deeds and the guardians could not be cleansed of their corruption.

Fennuk
Ah, the honeyed delight of a scheme well-played! Grimnir's is no more, and the final laugh is mine, ahaha!

Taukara, Daughter of War
We are what remain of the Northguard, the sons and daughters of those slain by Grimnir. Our guardians hath he subjugated to his will and caused us to lead bitter lives of sorrow and war. We wake this day with vengence upon our lips and justice etched upon our swords.

Balgair
The staff of Grimnir shall remain here, unmoved, until the Fox Guardians return.

Omol the Abandoned
The Northguard have forsaken this land and set sail across the sea. Yet again, I remain, unworthy to join them because of the crimes of my people.

Balgair
Grimnir, consumed by envy and hate, sought to corrupt the light of all the animal guardians.  One by one, he subjugated them to his will.  However, the Fox eluded him and fled far from this realm, never to be seen again.

Words of Memory
In ancient days, Éona, the mother of all, had many children. From them came the Fox Tribe, Bear Tribe, Ram Tribe, Wolf Tribe, Stag Tribe, and Raven Tribe. For hundreds of years the tribes lived in peace and each were blessed by the light of their animal guardians.

Balgair
Though, in nights calm light when dreams doth take me, I see our guardian run through the sky. The fox yet lives in lands far off and will return long after I have died.

Words of Memory
In ancient days, a fox came to this island from across the sea, running through the sky amidst the northern lights. Upon his back was a child called Éona, the last of the Aurorians. We are her decendants.
